knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=A data.frame of omic expression data with gene names in the rows ;; pdata=A phenotype data.frame containing at least "Sample" and "Class" columns ;; control_lab=A character string specifying the control class label in the Class column ;; pathways=An optional list of pathways/genesets (e.g., loaded via fgsea::gmtPathways) to calculate pathway-specific sample scores ;; fraction_genes=An option in the mdp function to control the top fraction of ranked genes that count as perturbed_genes ;; measure=Statistic used for normalization in z-score calculation; defaults to "median" (using MAD), can be set to "mean" ;; std=Threshold for z-score zeroing (default is 2) in compute_zscore
- alternatives: None mentioned, but the package expands on the Molecular Distance to Health algorithm implemented in Pankla et al. 2009 by adding modified z-scores, adjustable thresholds, and test-versus-control ranking.
- when_to_use: Use when you want to quantify the degree of molecular perturbation and heterogeneity of individual samples (e.g., clinical test samples) compared to a baseline control group, and identify which genes or pathways drive this perturbation.
- pitfalls: The phenotype data.frame (pdata) must contain columns named exactly "Sample" and "Class". The expression data.frame (data) must have gene names in the rows.

workflows.name: standard_mdp_analysis
workflows.intent: Quantify sample and gene perturbation scores relative to a control group using omic expression data.
input: expression_data.csv (omic data matrix with genes in rows)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the mdp package and input datasets ;; 2. Run the main mdp function to calculate perturbation scores ;; 3. Extract and plot sample scores for the perturbed genes ;; 4. Extract thresholded z-scores, gene scores, gene frequencies, and the list of perturbed genes.
workflows.code:
library(mdp)
data(example_data) # expression data has gene names in the rows
data(example_pheno) # pheno data needs a Sample and Class column
mdp.results <- mdp(data=example_data, pdata=example_pheno, control_lab = "baseline")
sample_scores_list <- mdp.results$sample_scores
sample_scores <- sample_scores_list[["perturbedgenes"]]
head(sample_scores)
sample_plot(sample_scores,control_lab = "baseline", title="perturbed")
zscore <- mdp.results$zscore
gene_scores <- mdp.results$gene_scores
gene_freq <- mdp.results$gene_freq
head(gene_scores)
perturbed_genes <- mdp.results$perturbed_genes

workflows.name: pathway_mdp_analysis
workflows.intent: Quantify sample perturbation scores within specific biological pathways using gene sets.
input: expression_data.csv (omic data matrix with genes in rows)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the mdp package and input datasets ;; 2. Read the pathway GMT file using fgsea::gmtPathways ;; 3. Run the mdp function with the pathways argument ;; 4. Extract pathway signal-to-noise ratios and pathway-specific sample scores ;; 5. Plot sample scores for a specific pathway.
workflows.code:
library(mdp)
data(example_data) # expression data has gene names in the rows
data(example_pheno) # pheno data needs a Sample and Class column
file_address <- system.file("extdata", "ReactomePathways.gmt", package = "mdp")
pathways <- fgsea::gmtPathways(file_address)
mdp.results <- mdp(data=example_data, pdata=example_pheno, control_lab = "baseline",pathways=pathways)
head(mdp.results$pathways)
sample_scores <- mdp.results$sample_scores[["Interferon alpha/beta signaling"]]
sample_plot(sample_scores,control_lab = "baseline", title="Interferon a/b")
